extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for organizations that regularly publish fact-checks, specifying values and operating expectations (e.g., nonpartisanship, transparency, sourcing, and regular reporting on public claims). Intended to inform how fact-checking organizations should conduct and present accuracy reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote excellence in fact-checking
rubrics_metrics.description: The IFCN at Poynter is committed to promoting excellence in fact-checking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code exists to encourage high standards among practitioners; excellence underpins the other principles and the network's mission to improve accountability journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpartisan fact-checking
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code is for organizations that regularly publish nonpartisan reports on the accuracy of statements by public figures, major institutions, and other widely circulated claims. Nonpartisanship is stated as essential because partisan work would undermine trust and the accountability role of fact-checking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent fact-checking
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasizes that nonpartisan and transparent fact-checking can be a powerful instrument of accountability journalism, implying transparency in methods, sources, and reasoning to build credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular publication of accuracy reports on public claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations should regularly publish reports on the accuracy of statements by public figures, major institutions, and other widely circulated claims of interest to society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code is intended for entities that make a sustained effort to evaluate public claims rather than one-off or occasional pieces; regularity and the focus on widely circulated/public-interest claims are explicit expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unsourced or biased fact-checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not produce unsourced or biased fact-checking, as this can increase distrust in the media and experts and pollute public understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page warns that unsourced or biased fact-checking harms public trust; therefore signatories should use reliable sourcing and guard against bias in research, presentation, and judgement.
